before: An R function that displays a representation of an object, often including position labels.
after: Display a value using R's usual printed form, which may include a position marker.

before: R’s usual leftward assignment operator; it stores the right-hand value under the left-hand name.
after: Give the name on the left the value from the right.

before: R code that computes a numeric result, such as score * 3.
after: A piece of code that works out a number.

before: An R branch controlled by a single non-missing logical value.
after: Use one condition to choose which block runs.

before: An R loop that repeats while its single condition remains TRUE.
after: Keep running a block while its condition is true.

before: An R object containing reusable instructions, parameters, and a returned result.
after: A named or unnamed set of instructions that can use inputs and give back an answer.

before: An R script run with explicit startup settings rather than silently relying on a prior interactive workspace.
after: A file of R instructions run in a fresh session without relying on a previously saved workspace.

before: A sequence whose elements share one atomic storage type.
after: An ordered collection whose entries share one basic type.

before: The L suffix requesting integer storage for a suitable R numeric literal.
after: An L after a whole number tells R to store that literal as an integer.

before: Repeating a shorter vector’s entries to align an operation with a longer vector, subject to the operation’s rules.
after: Reuse values from a shorter vector as needed to pair them with a longer vector.

before: Applying logical operations to corresponding vector positions rather than automatically reducing them to one condition.
after: Check a condition at each position and return one logical result for each pair.

before: Numbering the first element as position one.
after: Count the first position as one, not zero.

before: An R subscript that omits positions rather than selecting them from the end.
after: An index with a minus sign leaves out the position it names.

before: An index mask containing an unknown NA entry, which must not silently be treated as FALSE.
after: A selection test can contain NA. An unknown test can leave an unknown entry in the result.

before: A vector with a names attribute that can support character-based selection.
after: A vector whose entries have labels you can use to select them.

before: A missing, undefined or infinite numeric value that does not pass is.finite.
after: Infinity and NaN are not finite numbers. R's finite test also returns false for missing values.

before: The distinction between a length-zero null object and a missing value occupying a vector position.
after: NULL has length zero; a single NA occupies one position whose value is unknown.

before: Joining several result strings into a single character element using a separator.
after: Join several finished strings into one string, optionally separating them with a chosen mark.

before: Selecting a sub-list with [ or extracting one component with [[, which are different operations.
after: Use single brackets to keep a smaller list or double brackets to take out the item itself.

before: A table-like list of columns with a common row count, whose columns may have different types.
after: A table with rows and named columns. Columns can hold different types.

before: Simplifying a subset’s container shape, which can be prevented with an applicable drop=FALSE argument.
after: Selecting one column may give back a vector. drop=FALSE asks to keep the table shape.

before: An integer encoding of a category according to its factor levels, not necessarily the numeric meaning of its label.
after: The integer position of a category in a factor's list of levels. Its printed label can look very different.

before: The rule mapping a supplied vector into matrix row and column positions.
after: The direction in which input values fill a matrix. By default R fills down each column.

before: An index sequence such as seq_along(x) that correctly becomes empty for zero-length input.
after: A sequence containing only the positions that exist, including no positions for an empty vector.

before: An expression supplying a parameter when its argument is omitted, subject to R’s evaluation rules.
after: A value or expression used for an input when the caller leaves it out.

before: Resolving a name through the environment where a function was defined and its enclosing environments.
after: Look for a name in the current call and then in its enclosing environments.

before: An argument expression is evaluated when its promised value is needed.
after: An input whose value may not be worked out until the function needs it.

before: The ... formal collects unmatched arguments for inspection or forwarding.
after: Three dots can receive extra arguments and pass them to another function.

before: The retained environment used by a function to resolve nonlocal names.
after: A function keeps access to the environment where it was made.

before: Assigning an environment to another name preserves a reference to the same mutable environment.
after: Two names can refer to the same environment. A change made through one name is visible through the other.

before: Metadata attached to an R object that may affect interpretation or dispatch.
after: Extra information attached to an object, such as names or a unit label.

before: A function that selects an implementation using an object’s class.
after: A function that chooses a method using the class of its input.

before: A named component with a declared class in a formal S4 object.
after: A named part of an S4 object that must hold a value of the required type.

before: A tryCatch error handler replaces a failed expression’s result after control leaves the failing context.
after: Handle an error by leaving the failed calculation and supplying a result from the handler.

before: A handler invoked in the signaling context, permitting available restarts rather than automatically exiting the expression.
after: A handler that runs where a condition was signaled. It may allow that calculation to continue.

before: An expression registered with on.exit to run when its current function finishes or unwinds.
after: An action registered to run when the current function ends, even if it exits with an error.

before: vapply checks each result against an explicit length/type template.
after: Apply a function to items while checking each answer against a promised result type and length.

before: The dimension retained while apply processes slices along other dimensions.
after: The dimension you work across. In a matrix, margin one selects rows and two selects columns.

before: Partitioning observations by group and applying a summary with an explicit missing-value policy.
after: Separate values by group, apply a rule to each group, then collect the results.

before: The index sequence that reorders related values together without losing alignment.
after: A list of positions that puts entries into sorted order.

before: The number of matching row combinations created by repeated join keys.
after: The number of pairs made by a join. Every matching row on one side can pair with every matching row on the other.

before: A layout with explicit entity and occasion identifiers and a shared measurement column.
after: One row per measured value, with columns identifying what was measured and when.

before: R syntax that inserts a value into a subsequent function call.
after: Send the value on the left into the function call on the right.

before: Matching exact characters rather than interpreting regular-expression metacharacters.
after: Match characters as written instead of using them as pattern instructions.

before: Date arithmetic counts days, while POSIXct numeric offsets count seconds.
after: A Date counts calendar days. A date-time marks an instant that can be shown in different time zones.

before: Using package::export to select an installed package’s public object explicitly.
after: Use two colons to choose an exported name from a particular package.

before: Choosing an import type to preserve the domain meaning of each column.
after: Choose a column's type to fit what it means. An ID with leading zeros may need to stay text.

before: Saving and restoring one trusted R object with its R-specific structure.
after: Save an R object in a form that R can read back with its structure.

before: Assigning responsibility for closing an opened stream on every exit path.
after: The code that opens a connection is responsible for making sure it closes.

before: Turning a tolerance-based comparison into an explicit pass/fail condition.
after: Test whether two numbers are close enough for an allowed tolerance.

before: Repeating a pseudorandom operation from a known generator state.
after: Reset the same random generator to the same starting state to repeat a sample with the same settings.

before: A numerical description of where a distribution is centered, chosen for a specific purpose.
after: One number describing the center of data, such as the mean or median.

before: Variation measures must be interpreted with their scaling and unit conventions.
after: A measure of how far apart values are. Standard deviation and interquartile range use the original measurement units.

before: Model probability that a random value is at or below a threshold.
after: The probability that a value is at or below a chosen point.

before: A parameter-interval method with coverage defined over repeated sampling under assumptions.
after: A method for making a range from a sample. Its confidence level describes how often the method covers the true value across repeated samples under its assumptions.

before: Tail evidence computed under a null model, not the probability a hypothesis is true.
after: A p-value measures how unusual a result this extreme or more would be if the tested claim and assumptions held.

before: A relationship among observed values does not by itself identify the effect of an intervention.
after: A pattern between two measurements does not by itself show that one caused the other.

before: A symbolic declaration of response and predictor terms rather than ordinary arithmetic evaluation.
after: A rule describing what to predict and which inputs to use for the prediction.

before: Uncertainty in an estimated mean differs from uncertainty for a new individual response.
after: An interval for a single future value allows for individual variation as well as uncertainty about the mean.

before: Examining observed-minus-fitted discrepancies for model problems without treating a single check as proof.
after: Inspect the differences between observations and fitted predictions to look for patterns the model missed.

before: The category against which other factor levels are compared in treatment-coded coefficients.
after: The group used as the starting point for comparing other groups.

before: The model linear-predictor scale differs from the scale of the modeled mean.
after: A logistic model can give a result as log-odds on its link scale or as a probability on its response scale.

before: Opening, drawing to and closing an output target to finalize a graphical artifact.
after: Open a drawing destination, draw to it, and close it so the output is finished.

before: Explicit boundaries and endpoint inclusion determine which observations enter each bin.
after: Bin edges and rules about including their endpoints decide which values a histogram counts together.

before: Improving observed performance while preserving results and accounting for measurement conditions.
after: Compare measured work before claiming a speed improvement. Timing can vary between runs.

before: Evaluating authored language objects differs from safely interpreting untrusted data.
after: Evaluating a saved expression runs code. Use expressions from a trusted source; choosing an environment is not a security sandbox.

before: Recording and controlling relevant runtime, dependency and configuration state.
after: Record the R setup and restore temporary settings so later work is not silently changed.

before: Explicit accepted types, values and result limits before computing a descriptive summary.
after: Check the input, limit how many valid values to keep, and handle an empty result before summarizing.
